title: lmkd 架构：PSI/vmpressure、kill strategy 与关键属性
key_conclusions: lmkd reacts to pressure and chooses victims, but it is not a complete root-cause attribution system.
PSI is the preferred modern pressure input, while vmpressure remains a compatibility path on some devices.
Victim selection depends on oom_score_adj, memory cost, policy properties, and pressure state.
Day 53 bucket attribution is still required to distinguish victim responsibility from shared or system pressure.
shallow_points: The article does not validate exact lmkd property names and defaults across Android releases and vendors.
It does not include real lmkd log lines from devices under controlled PSI pressure.
It does not quantify kill thresholds for low-RAM and normal-RAM products.
It does not show a full statsd atom example for low-memory kills.
discovered_connections: Day 53 explains source buckets, while Day 54 explains the pressure-response daemon that acts after pressure is high.
Day 52 PSI windows are the bridge between kernel stalls and lmkd pressure callbacks.
OomAdjuster is the next required topic because lmkd trusts oom_score_adj when selecting victims.
Shared dma-buf or slab pressure can make lmkd kill a process that did not create the dominant source bucket.
suggest_future_topics: Day 55 should explain ActivityManager OomAdjuster and how process state becomes oom_score_adj.
